title: EscApp — Windows games on your Mac
description: EscApp runs Windows games on Apple Silicon Macs and sets everything up by itself. Open the game and play.
hero_title: Windows games on your Mac. Open it and play.
hero_lead: EscApp runs Windows games on Apple Silicon and does all the work itself. It figures out what the game needs, finds the settings it runs best with and remembers them. Nothing to set up, nothing to think about: open the game and play.
requirements: Free and open source · macOS 15 or later · Apple Silicon
how_lead: You do one thing: open the game. Everything else is EscApp's job. No settings to pick, no guides to read, no Windows to install.
step1_text: Double-click its .exe in Finder, or drop the game's folder on EscApp. Installers work too.
step2_text: It looks at the game, sets up everything it needs and tries settings until the game runs well. On its own, while you wait a moment.
step3_text: The settings that worked are remembered, so from then on the game simply starts.
shots_lead: The whole app is a library of your games. There is nothing else to learn.
library_alt: The EscApp library before any games are added, with three steps: find the game, double-click its .exe, start playing
library_caption: Open a game once and it lives here, one click from playing.
setup_alt: EscApp's first start: it downloads what Windows games need, with a progress bar for each part
setup_caption: The first start downloads what games need. It happens once, by itself.
features_title: Made to stay out of your way
features_lead: Everything a Windows game expects is handled for you, quietly.
directx_text: EscApp reads the game and picks how to draw it on Metal. If the first choice fails, it tries the next.
components_text: Visual C++, .NET and RPG Maker's run time packages come from their publishers, only when a game needs them.
saves_text: All games share one profile, so saves and settings stay put however many games you add.
scaling_text: Games built for small screens are enlarged smoothly instead of switching your Mac's display.
japanese_text: Games made for Japanese Windows start with the right language and fonts, so the text reads correctly.
private_text: Nothing about you or your games is sent anywhere. Every download is checked against a pinned fingerprint. The code is Apache-2.0.
status_lead: Free and open source. More games and features arrive with every update.
works_text: DirectX 9–11 games, Unity games, RPG Maker XP/VX/VX Ace, games that need Visual C++ or .NET.
stores_text: Steam and Epic Games Store install with one button.
needs_text: a Mac with Apple Silicon and macOS 15 or later.
footer: EscApp is open source under Apache-2.0. Wine, DXVK and DXMT are separate projects under their own licences.
dx_description: How to add Apple's D3DMetal to EscApp, so DirectX 12 games run on your Mac.
dx_lead: DirectX 12 games run on D3DMetal, Apple's own translation of DirectX 12 to Metal. Apple doesn't allow EscApp to include it, but you can download it from Apple yourself, for free. It takes a couple of minutes, once.
dx_needs_account: An Apple Account. A free one is enough: no paid developer membership.
dx_needs_space: About 100 MB of free space: the download is about 25 MB, and D3DMetal takes about 65 MB.
dx_step1_text: Open Settings › DirectX 12. When a DirectX 12 game can't start, EscApp offers the same screen with Set Up DirectX 12…
dx_step2_text:
1. Click Open Apple's Download Page in EscApp: it opens in your browser.
2. Sign in with your Apple Account (Apple ID). A free account is enough, no paid developer membership. The first time, Apple asks you to agree to its developer terms; that's free too.
3. In the list, find Evaluation environment for Windows games 3.0 (blue icon) or a newer one. Not Game Porting Toolkit (red icon): that's a different download.
4. Click View Details under it, then Evaluation_environment_for_Windows_games_3.0.dmg (about 25 MB). Don't open the file.
dx_step3_text: EscApp finds the file in your Downloads folder by itself and shows a button with its name: click it. Saved it somewhere else? Click Choose File… or drag the file onto the steps in EscApp. EscApp checks that the file really comes from Apple; nothing is added yet.
dx_step4_text: EscApp shows the license that came with the file. Click Agree and Add. That's all: DirectX 12 games now start like any other.
dx_license_text: D3DMetal is Apple's software. You accept Apple's license when you download it, and your use of it is between you and Apple: Apple gives it out for developing, testing and evaluating games. EscApp doesn't include, sell or change it; it copies D3DMetal from your download after checking Apple's signature and shows you Apple's license first. If you're unsure whether the license fits how you use it, don't add it.
dx_trouble_wrong_a: You chose another download from Apple's page. Download “Evaluation environment for Windows games”.
dx_trouble_signed_a: The file is damaged or didn't come from Apple. Download it again from Apple's page.
dx_trouble_game_q: A DirectX 12 game still doesn't start
dx_trouble_game_a: Not every DirectX 12 game works with D3DMetal yet, and games with kernel-level anti-cheat don't run on a Mac at all. Copy Report in the window that says the game didn't start tells what happened.
dx_trouble_remove_q: How do I update or remove it?
dx_trouble_remove_a: In Settings › DirectX 12: Replace… takes a newer download from Apple, Remove deletes D3DMetal from your Mac.
